definition.description: From a bilateral standing hinge with an intact slam ball held low near the hips or between the legs, drive through the hips and legs, accelerate the ball in an underhand scoop path, redirect it into a marked floor target, then use the declared dead-ball retrieval or controlled catch reset. This excludes an overhead-start slam, a scoop throw, a shuffle-entry slam, a slam-to-scoop combination, rotational release, or a rebound-catch objective.

environment.surface: dry stable non-slip impact-suitable floor with a clear low scoop arc, marked floor target, and protected rebound/retrieval zone
environment.space: one athlete at a time; no people or fragile objects in the scoop, release, rebound, or retrieval path
inspection: confirm intact impact-rated ball and dry impact-suitable floor
confirm low start, scoop arc, target, front/overhead clearance, and retrieval route
confirm grip, footwear, communication, and stop route
environment.changeRule: Changing start height, hinge, ball construction or mass, scoop path, target, release, rebound/catch rule, entry, cadence, dose, or purpose requires revalidation.

selectionPrerequisites: safe bilateral hinge, grip, hip-led scoop, controlled redirection, and clear impact/retrieval zone
can follow the declared retrieval or controlled catch rule
current posterior-chain, shoulder, grip, ballistic hinge, and session-fatigue budgets fit
understands target, reset, and stop signal
excludeOrEscalate: symptom, restriction, unsafe ball, floor, arc, target, rebound/retrieval, spacing, or communication conflict
pain, loss of grip, dizziness, neurologic, circulation, breathing, chest, balance, or communication concern
notEstablishedByEvidence: universal ball mass, start height, range, recovery, readiness threshold, output, or clinical clearance

provenance.identityAuthority: Source 1164 plus ball-slam-foundations-v1 evidence packet. Exact low-start scoop-to-floor mechanics remain candidate-only pending coach identity confirmation; no candidate media is assumed exact.

anatomy.laterality: bilateral symmetric standing base and two-hand ball handling
anatomy.claimsBoundary: Task mechanics and likely loading sites only; no diagnosis, treatment, injury-prevention, isolated activation, or guaranteed performance claim.

athleteSupport.whyItMatters: Candidate low-start hip-led ballistic ball exposure when this exact scoop-to-floor path fits the workout.
athleteSupport.primaryCue: Start low with hips loaded, drive the floor away, scoop fast, redirect into the floor target, and reset safely.
secondaryCues: do not turn the scoop into a free throw
keep the target and retrieval path clear
use a ball that stays fast and controllable
end before the back or arms take over
expectedSensations: brief hip, leg, trunk, shoulder, and grip effort
high-intent scoop followed by deliberate reset
unexpectedSensations: back, hip, shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand, knee, or foot pain
loss of grip, uncontrolled throw vector, unsafe rebound, dizziness, or loss of balance
selfChecks: ball redirects to the marked floor target
assigned catch or retrieval is controlled

observationChecklist: exact low-start scoop-to-floor identity, not overhead slam, scoop throw, rotational slam, shuffle entry, or rebound-catch objective
ball construction/mass, target, clearance, spacing, rebound and retrieval route
hinge, hip extension, scoop path, trunk, grip, redirection, target accuracy, symptoms, and first quality loss

faultCorrections.arm_only_scoop_or_slow_path: reduce ball mass or repetitions, restore hinge-to-hip extension timing, and end when speed does not return
faultCorrections.lumbar_extension_or_early_throw: reduce range/intensity, restore rib-pelvis organization and floor target, or stop
faultCorrections.target_drift_or_unsafe_rebound: reset the target and retrieval rule; do not count or continue uncontrolled releases

doNotUseWhen: an overhead-start, free scoop throw, rotational, shuffle-entry, slam-to-scoop, or mandatory rebound-catch task is intended
ball, floor, target, clearance, rebound/retrieval path, or communication is unsafe
the exact task conflicts with symptoms, restrictions, or current ballistic-hinge fatigue budget

supportOperations.supportEscalation: Stop unresolved equipment, target, identity, symptom, or quality concerns and follow facility escalation policy.
supportOperations.changeImpactPolicy: Any change to start, hinge, ball, mass, path, target, release, rebound/catch, cadence, dose, or substitution reruns selection, logistics, duration, fatigue, substitutions, and validation.

dosage.countRule: count only low-start hip-led scoops that redirect to the assigned floor target with declared catch/retrieval and full reset

deliveryProfiles.qualityGate: Every counted rep retains the exact low start, hinge-to-extension timing, scoop path, stable trunk and grip, marked floor target, safe retrieval rule, and no stop event.
stopRules: stop on pain, loss of grip, uncontrolled throw vector, unsafe ball/floor/clearance/rebound/retrieval zone, loss of balance, or participant request
stop when speed, target accuracy, low-start path, trunk organization, or safe retrieval cannot be restored
stop after two slow or mistargeted reps rather than converting this into conditioning
deliveryProfiles.coachInstructions: Inspect ball, floor, target, scoop arc, clearance, and retrieval zone; declare mass, start/path, catch/retrieval, count, and rest; observe side and front views and stop at the first unrecoverable quality loss.
deliveryProfiles.athleteInstructions: Start low with the assigned ball, hinge, drive through the hips, scoop it up, redirect it into the marked floor target, then retrieve or catch it as assigned before resetting.
deliveryProfiles.expectedAdaptation: Candidate task-specific low-start ballistic ball exposure only; no universal power, sport, or injury outcome is guaranteed.

doseScaling.doNotAutoProgress: Do not add shuffle entry, overhead start, rotation, free throw, slam-to-scoop sequence, mandatory rebound catch, or conditioning volume without revalidation.
